outcome: Coagulation potential (assessed by coagulography and thromboelastography)
Volume of blood loss during childbirth and early postpartum period
Risk of complications of neuraxial blockade
cohort: The study involved 70 patients undergoing delivery, divided into a main group with gestational thrombocytopenia (35 patients) and a comparison group with normal platelet count (35 patients).
finding: In patients with gestational thrombocytopenia, even with a significant decrease in platelet content (above 49x10^9/l), neuraxial blockades can be safely performed during labor, as there is no decrease in coagulation potential and no increased risk of blood loss or complications compared to those without thrombocytopenia.
mod_finding: The volume of blood loss did not differ between groups regardless of the method of delivery (vaginal or abdominal).
